title: Design a Shared Calendar Sync Platform
prompt: Design shared calendars with event CRUD, interval queries, user/group sharing, recurrence and exceptions, multi-device sync, time zones, and concurrent edits. Cover ACL enforcement, version conflicts, ordered changes, recurrence expansion, notifications, and failure handling.

response.placeholder: Store recurrence rules and exceptions, not an infinite set of instances. Define the stale-edit response.
response.reference_answer:
## Model and access
Events carry calendar ID, owner, ACL version, time-zone-aware timestamps, recurrence rule, exceptions, and optimistic version. Group membership is resolved before reads/writes; a stale edit returns a conflict instead of silently overwriting.

## Query and recurrence
Index bounded interval overlap queries by calendar/time. Store recurrence rules and materialize only a requested range, applying overrides/cancellations; background expansion can warm near-term instances but is not authority.

## Sync
Append durable ordered changes per calendar and expose cursor-based delta sync. Push notifications only hint clients to fetch changes. A device reconnects from cursor or takes a fresh snapshot when compacted.

## Progressive Hints
1. Time zones belong in recurrence semantics.
2. Push is not a consistency protocol.
3. ACL changes invalidate cached authorization.
